title: Roadmap | ContextMint
description: ContextMint product roadmap — v1.0 end of August 2026, v2.0 Engineering Intelligence Platform, Track B enterprise and compliance, plus Verification Engine direction.

hero.title: Roadmap
hero.leadHtml: Three horizons: v1.0 pilots the decision-control plane now (GA end of August 2026); v2.0 unifies engineering intelligence on one Knowledge Fabric; Track B extends the same core to org-wide knowledge with enterprise controls. Directional — not a delivery schedule.

horizons.title: Decision-control plane
horizons.text: Engine, Context Lens, quality map, federated governance lookup — GA end of August 2026.

horizons.title: Engineering Intelligence Platform
horizons.text: Knowledge Fabric, institutional memory, CHRONOS, operational intelligence retrieval.

horizons.title: Enterprise & compliance
horizons.text: Jira, Confluence, SharePoint, Git, and org knowledge — plus SSO, RBAC, and audit.

glance.title: At a glance
glance.footerHtml: Capabilities and order evolve with design partner feedback. We label shipping vs planned explicitly — no certification or autonomous-governance claims.

v1.title: Decision-control plane
v1.introHtml: Local-first decision-control plane for software teams — evidence before inference, human approval before repo changes. In internal pilot now; design partner intake opens by start of September 2026. General availability end of August 2026.
items: ContextMint Engine — tray-native operator console (server, Ollama, models, indexing, quality scans, logs, support bundle)
VS Code extension — Ask / Plan / Agent modes, context lanes (Repo / Work / Hybrid), chat sessions, attach context, suggested prompts
Context Lens (gate 1) — preview retrieved chunks, scores, routing, and governance notes before the model runs
Patch preview (gate 2) — review unified diffs before anything applies; no silent writes
Quality map — stored governance findings (clones, near-duplicates, structure signals) with optional apply gates
Federated query router v0.1 — governance lookup reads the Findings Store first (store-first, tier-agnostic facts, trust metadata) — not chat-time rediscovery
Context packs — per-repo manifests with @pack:name activation and auto-sync
Glass-box routing — provenance breakdown, routing badge, reasoning trace for power users
Conventions learner — proposals and audit history with human approval before rules enter the graph
Image evidence — paste UI screenshots in chat; local Ollama vision by default; Context Lens preview before send
ARGUS visual audit — structured WCAG-tagged findings on screenshots; report only, human-gated fixes
Workspace-agnostic evidence assembly — index-time route knowledge when available, then hybrid search + expand (file windows, grep, dependency graph) on any indexed repo
Symbol-aware retrieval — citations name file, symbol, and line range — not anonymous text chunks
Local-first default — Engine + Ollama on loopback; code stays on device
v1.footerHtml: Optional (off by default): BYOK cloud routing, git sandbox worktrees, inline completion, shared on-prem API server for enterprise pilots — full v1.0 list.

designPartners.title: 2026 pilot cohort
designPartners.introHtml: A 30-day evaluation pilot is a bounded proof-of-concept — not a product subscription limit. After onboarding, 10–30 developers on one team or repo use ContextMint in real work for one calendar month; we review together and deliver a written summary for security and platform leadership. Extendable to 90 days when the pilot is going well.
noticeItems: Week 0 — install Engine + extension; index one repo; security path agreed
Weeks 1–4 — daily dev usage with Context Lens and patch preview gates
Week 2 & 4 — short async feedback (email or form — no standing meetings required)
End of month — pilot summary report + go / extend / stop decision
designPartners.bodyHtml: You get direct engineering access; we get honest signal on fit for regulated and sovereign AI dev workflows — and priority input on v2.0 and Track B (including which knowledge systems to connect first).
items: Guided pilot playbook — week-2 and week-4 feedback (async OK)
Deployment path review — local Engine per developer or shared on-prem server (deployment models)
Security questionnaire support — architecture summaries for stakeholders
Priority input — influence v2.0 Fabric scope and Track B enterprise packaging
Team rollout patterns — Docker / Helm shared-server pilots with platform engineering
Pilot summary report — outcomes for security and engineering leadership

v2.title: Engineering Intelligence Platform
v2.introHtml: After v1.0 exit, ContextMint becomes one living digital twin of the engineering system — not seven siloed tools. Retrieval, memory, health analysis, temporal forensics, and multimodal validation become query projections over a single logical model: the Knowledge Fabric. Starts post–v1.0 freeze; target MVP first quarter of 2027 (Q1).
v2.philosophyHtml: Philosophy: Do not build 7 tools. Build 1 Fabric — users experience Memory Tab, Architecture Console, CHRONOS bisect, ORACLE prefetch, ARGUS audit, and MESH delegation as surfaces; engineers maintain one ingestion pipeline and one schema.

waves.title: Wave 1 — Institutional memory
waves.text: Fabric shadow-write, learner approval gate, Memory Tab — conventions become graph nodes with evidence.

waves.title: Wave 2 — Temporal & structural
waves.text: CHRONOS checkpoint forensics, health analysis, Architecture Tab — graph/metadata first, not commit embeddings.

waves.title: Wave 3 — Zero-latency UX
waves.text: ORACLE prefetch — intent + retrieval context cached before you ask; extends v1 PERF layers.

waves.title: Wave 4 — Multimodal validation
waves.text: ARGUS audit reports in sandbox — structured findings, human reviews fixes separately.

waves.title: Wave 5 — Distributed compute (lite)
waves.text: MESH-Lite — explicit trusted peers for heavy VLM/health jobs; no auto-discovery swarm.

waves.title: Wave 6 — conditional
waves.text: Full mesh only if Wave 5 proves measurable runtime benefit in dogfood.

v2.oiIntroHtml: v1.0 assembles named engineering artifacts with index-time knowledge objects (routes today), hybrid search + expand, and human gates. v2.0 adds scoring belief across more object kinds — and reconciles conflicting signals into one auditable answer.
oiItems: Knowledge reconciliation — when Git, CODEOWNERS, team memory, and docs disagree, surface one scored claim with supporting and conflicting evidence
Operational intelligence retrieval (OIR) — rank by relevance and trust, freshness, and evidence coverage
Domain-aware retrieval — files and symbols tagged to domains; filter by ownership and architectural boundaries, not chunks alone
Repository DNA + Feature Registry Lite — deterministic health baselines and feature traceability on the Fabric
Summary-first retrieval — semantic compression at index time; expand to raw code only when confidence is low
RBAC + audit foundations — tenant_id / owner_id on Fabric nodes; immutable audit schema (full enterprise packaging continues in Track B)
v2.footerHtml: We do not claim trust-weighted retrieval or cross-system reconciliation until product gates pass. v1.0 already ships index-time route knowledge, store-first governance lookup, and symbol-aware citations. Glossary →

trackB.title: Enterprise & organizational knowledge
trackB.introHtml: Track B extends ContextMint from developer code intelligence into an explainable organizational knowledge platform — same retrieval core and local-first posture, with security and compliance controls that regulated buyers require. Builds on the v2.0 Fabric; target MVP end of 2027. After design partner intake opens, cohort feedback will help prioritize which external systems to connect first.
trackB.noticeHtml: Connected knowledge (Track B): One governed index across the systems your teams already use — not code in isolation. v1.0 indexes Git repos today; Track B adds adapter-based ingest for Jira (issues, epics, ownership), Confluence (wikis, ADRs, runbooks), SharePoint (document libraries, policies), Git (multi-repo and org-wide code graph), and other knowledge bases (Notion, internal portals, ticket systems — partner-driven priority). Answers cite the source system with ACL respected per document.
securityItems: Foundation controls (B0) — unified authorization on every read path; cache keys scoped to tenant + role; explainable score breakdown fields
Security boundary (B3) — document-level ACL enforcement; hard multi-tenant isolation (scoped storage roots, per-tenant keys, no cross-tenant joins)
External knowledge adapters (B1+) — Jira, Confluence, SharePoint, Git org-graph, and partner-selected knowledge bases; async ingest queue with ACL from each source
Document ingestion (B1) — PDF, DOCX, and exported wiki pages with async queue, backpressure, and quarantine for OCR-heavy workloads
Metadata + PII (B2) — policy-driven redaction modes; metadata boosts bounded so base retrieval ranking stays stable and explainable
Enterprise surface (B4) — OIDC/SAML SSO, API gateway policies, admin console for roles, retention, index health, and audit browsing
Compliance packaging (B5) — GDPR deletion proof, air-gapped Helm/Docker bundles, tamper-evident audit (hash-chain + signed checkpoints), SOC 2 evidence collectors
outcomes: Ask questions across code + Jira + Confluence + SharePoint — one answer with cited evidence, not four conflicting snippets
One platform for engineering and internal docs — same Context Lens and human-gate model
Team server deployment with SSO — extension connects to shared on-prem API, not loopback-only
Compliance exports your security team can run without vendor workshops
No cloud egress unless explicitly enabled per workspace or tenant
trackB.footerHtml: We do not claim live Jira/Confluence/SharePoint connectors, SOC 2 certification, or FedRAMP until gated. Adapter order follows design-partner demand; v1.0 pilots stay Git-first. Security use cases → · Co-shape Track B →

verification.title: Verification Engine
verification.introHtml: Longer-horizon capabilities on top of the Fabric — deterministic graph evidence first; AI narrates with citations, never overrides graph truth without human confirmation. Timing evolves with design partner feedback; many items follow Track B (end 2027) and extend into 2028+.
items: PR verification gates — ownership, impact, and policy checked on every change (vision)
Blast radius — graph traversal for impacted services, files, and teams (learn more)
Repository DNA — deterministic repo health and convention baselines (learn more)
Decision graph — architecture intent and ADR traceability (learn more)
Drift detection — scorecards for accepted vs violation baselines (learn more)
Agent governance — policy-scoped tool contracts for AI agents in CI (learn more)
ARGUS insights tab — cross-session audit history and team dashboards (beyond v1 paste + sandbox)
Enterprise CLI packaging — graph queries and verification in CI pipelines
MCP server for agents — blast radius, features, and decisions as tool contracts (contracts)
CI/CD deployment graph — pipeline and release context linked to code changes (after Track B knowledge fabric)

footer.textHtml: Capabilities and order may change as we learn from pilots. What ships in v1.0 is documented on Features. Governance and compliance claims follow our trust center — we do not promise autonomous governance or certification.

cta.title: Shape what ships next
cta.text: When design partner intake opens (start of September 2026), partners get a direct line to product engineering — especially for v2.0 Fabric scope and Track B requirements.
